Beat 1 of 5 14s · cumulative 0:14

Setup, what this is and who uses it

Beat 1 · Setup

Talk track

Here's IND Forge. The app preclinical teams use to build the Investigational New Drug application, better known as the IND, which is submitted to the FDA before dosing the first human. It pulls together every piece of evidence the agency needs to clear that first dose: animal pharmacology, toxicology, manufacturing, the proposed starting dose.

Presenter notes

  • Plain-English opener. Define IND once, up front, then move on. Everything after assumes the audience has it.
  • Gesture cue: sweep across the header strip (compound INDF-127, IND target Q4 2026, Phase 1 trial). Audience reads it; you don't have to.
  • Land "to dose the first human". That threshold is what every clinical person in the room understands intuitively. It's the moment.
Look at: The five stat cards (8 candidates, MOFA+ 10 factors, 1000 bootstraps 95% CI, Cambridge HPC cpu-long, 134 min wall time); the translatability envelope table with CI bars
Beat 2 of 5 16s · cumulative 0:30

The HPC step, multi-omics with confidence intervals

Beat 2 · The HPC step

Talk track

The compute-heavy step is integrating multi-omics across the animal cohort to confirm which biomarkers actually translate to humans, and to put confidence intervals around that translation so reviewers know how much to trust it. We're talking hundreds of CPU-hours per run, and the team needs to rerun it as new data comes in.

Presenter notes

  • The CI bars are the proof. Don't claim "we ran a bootstrap". Let the bars speak. Each candidate has a point estimate and a 95% interval.
  • 134 min · Cambridge HPC is visible at top-right. Sets up the next beat without you having to say it.
  • Pace fast. The audience doesn't need to read every row. Move on.
Look at: The amber residency callout in the Data Sources card and the "What this tab is for" copy block at top, both explicitly state the residency rule
Beat 3 of 5 15s · cumulative 0:45

The catch, animal data behind the firewall

Beat 3 · The catch

Talk track

But here's the catch. Animal data lives behind the firewall, on-prem only, by IT policy. Routing it to the cloud triggers a six-week data-transfer review every single time, and that's a non-starter for a team trying to hit an IND target. So the obvious answer, "just send it to the cloud and run it there," doesn't work.

Presenter notes

  • The screen says it for you. The amber callout: "All animal-omics is restricted to on-prem storage by IT policy. Cloud routing triggers a six-week data-transfer review." Point at it.
  • Tonal shift: drop voice slightly on "by IT policy". That's the constraint nobody can argue with. Land it as fact, not opinion.
  • Don't elaborate. This is the catch. Let it sit. Don't explain who, why, or what kind of review. Move to the answer.
Look at: Cambridge HPC selected as RECOMMENDED with the green compliance pills (Animal-omics data residency · Internal IT approved · GLP audit chain preserved)
Beat 4 of 5 14s · cumulative 0:59

The SLURM moment, compute moves to the data

Beat 4 · The SLURM moment

Talk track

This is where SLURM in Domino comes in. The same workload routes directly to the on-prem cluster where the animal data already lives. The job runs there, the results come back, and the data itself never crosses the firewall. The data doesn't move. The compute moves to it.

Presenter notes

  • Land the keeper line: "The data doesn't move. The compute moves to it." Pause briefly after. This is the sentence that survives.
  • Compliance pills do the work. Animal-omics data residency · Internal IT approved · GLP audit chain preserved, visible on Cambridge HPC. Don't read aloud; let them be seen.
  • No need to define SLURM. The cluster names (Cambridge HPC, NJ Research) and the on-prem framing are enough context.
Look at: The Bridging Evidence pill linking to the sweep run; the FIH starting dose 0.8 mg MABEL-controlled; the live derived-value panel with HED, MRSD, MABEL, exposure margin
Beat 5 of 5 13s · cumulative 1:12

The seam, pharmacometrician picks up the trail

Beat 5 · The seam

Talk track

Then the pharmacometrician picks up that exact same evidence trail to compute the first-in-human starting dose. Same run, same lineage, fully auditable end to end, and none of it ever left the on-prem environment. One audit chain, no egress.

Presenter notes

  • The Bridging Evidence pill is the seam visible. Links back to SWEEP-2026-05-03-A. Same run, same trail, picked up by the next persona.
  • Live math is the proof. HED, MRSD, MABEL, exposure margin, all derived from inputs, formulas shown with FDA 2005 / EMA 2017 §4.4 citations. A pharmacometrician sees this and respects it.
  • Final line is the keeper: "One audit chain, no egress." Three words. Stop talking after.
